evidence.excerpt:
LLM agents that interact with a user across many sessions accumulate histories
that exceed their context window, so they store past interactions in an external
memory and answer each question from a small set of retrieved records. Existing
memory systems rank records by lexical or embedding relevance, yet the top-
ranked memories can each be relevant while jointly omitting a complementary
fact that the answer requires, especially for multi-session and temporal questions.
Drawing on the distinction between relevance and sufficiency in legal evidence
scholarship, we recast memory retrieval as constructing asufficient memory set.
To operationalize this view, we introduce a blinded LLM judgment over the re-
trieved set, together with Gold Hit and Turn Hit as evidence-coverage proxies.
We then proposeBudgeted Flat Reconstruction (BFR), which builds sufficient
sets over a fixed flat memory

evidence.excerpt:
contributions:
(i) We formulate memory retrieval as the construction of a sufficient memory set and make set-level
sufficiency measurable: LLM-Suff@Set judges whether a retrieved set supports the answer, while
Gold Hit and Turn Hit track coverage of annotated answer-bearing evidence.
(ii) We propose BFR, a two-stage method for building sufficient sets over a flat memory. Its two
stages recover complementary evidence missing within and beyond the initial candidates.
(iii) We conduct extensive experiments on LOCOMOand LONGMEMEVAL-S. These results show
that BFR improves answer quality and evidence coverage, and identify where additional evidence is
recovered and clarify the distinct roles of evidence composition and acquisition.

harana et al., 2024) tests understanding of long, multi-session conversations, including questions
that require linking information across turns. LONGMEMEVAL-S (Wu et al., 2025) tests whether
a memory system can answer questions about information distributed across extended interaction
histories and sessions. Both provide evidence annotations, allowing us to assess retrieval as well as
final answers. To keep multi-arm evaluation costs manageable, we use a fixed stratified200-question
LOCOMOdevelopment subset; we evaluate all500questions of LONGMEMEVAL-S. Dataset prove-
nance and the construction of every derived evaluation subset are documented in Appendix G.

M ANNOTATION PROTOCOL
Suff@Set is labelled on a question–evidence snapshot rather than on the system answer. The blinded
input contains the question, reference answer, and anonymized evidence text; it withholds the
method, budget, system answer, and gold evidence identifiers. Two independent judges (gpt-5.5
andclaude-sonnet-4-6) assignsufficient,insufficient, oruncertain;gpt-6-soladjudicates
disagreements. All calls use temperature zero. Because the protocol includes the reference answer
and uses model judges, Suff@Set is an LLM-only, reference-conditioned offline evaluation measure
rather than a human annotation or an inference-time stopping signal. An uncertain or missing final
label is excluded from the binary-rate denominator; the originally reported FCA-MS, BFR-Text C3,
and BFR-MV C6 pilot produced no uncertain labels. No human Suff@Set labels are reported.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective benchmark annotations (Gold Hit, Turn Hit, CER) and Porter stem F1 corroborate the reported gains, with BFR-MV reaching 91.4% Turn Hit and 82.2% judged accuracy on LONGMEMEVAL-S.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by blinded reference-conditioned LLM judges (gpt-5.5 answer judge and Suff@Set adjudication) alongside benchmark ground-truth metrics including Porter stem F1, Gold Hit, Turn Hit, and Complete Evidence Recall.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system is shaped by fixed, rule-based and LLM-prompted heuristics: requirement decomposition, FCA prefiltering, minimal-subset selection, and budget-exhaustion stopping. No model weights are tuned against downstream judges.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported gains over same-store adaptations of Mem0, A-Mem, CoM, and MRAgent-Flat are well aligned with evidence, showing consistent improvements in answer accuracy and evidence coverage, while acknowledging that structured graph memories still exhibit higher associative precision.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation conducts rigorous same-store comparisons on LOCOMO and LONGMEMEVAL-S, holding the store, extractive answerer, and judge fixed. Headline claims are tracked across answer quality metrics (Porter stem F1, LLM judge) alongside independent benchmark annotations (Gold Hit, Turn Hit, CER).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Objective reference-based metrics including Porter stem F1, Gold Hit, Turn Hit, and Complete Evidence Recall directly corroborate the headline gains across both benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Blinded reference-conditioned LLM judgment (gpt-5.5 mem0 accuracy and Suff@Set adjudication) alongside ground-truth benchmark metrics (Porter stem F1, Gold Hit, Turn Hit, Evidence Recall).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Rule-based and LLM-prompted heuristic procedures (question requirement decomposition, FCA prefiltering, and fixed budget exhaustion stopping rules) without model weight tuning against downstream judges.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly disclose development contact on LOCOMO conversations, boundary differences when compared to non-flat graph architectures, and the failure of gold-free sufficiency estimates to act as viable dynamic stopping signals.
primary.method_assessment: The method is clearly specified: Stage I expands retrieval, decomposes queries into requirements, pre-filters via Formal Concept Analysis, and selects a minimal complementary subset grounded to turns; Stage II iteratively collects unseen records using fixed access schedules under an explicit budget limit.
primary.quality_rationale: The contribution is soundly scoped and executed, offering clear formalization, thorough empirical benchmarking, and rigorous ablations without overstating the capacity of flat stores against structured graphs.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formulates long-term memory retrieval as constructing a sufficient evidence set and introduces Budgeted Flat Reconstruction (BFR), combining formal concept analysis subset selection (FCA-MS) with budgeted multi-view or text-deepening completion over a flat memory store.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The contribution is soundly scoped and executed, offering clear formalization, thorough empirical benchmarking, and rigorous ablations without overstating the capacity of flat stores against structured graphs.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly disclose development contact on LOCOMO conversations, boundary differences when compared to non-flat graph architectures, and the failure of gold-free sufficiency estimates to act as viable dynamic stopping signals.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
